one_liner: Design tool that turns rough wireframes into responsive layout systems and exports real CSS Grid — no absolute positioning.
description: gridframe is a layout-first design tool. You sketch rough frames, and it resolves them into a responsive grid system with proper breakpoints, then exports clean CSS Grid and Flexbox that engineers will actually keep. It focuses on the layout layer that design-to-code tools get wrong, and audits existing designs for overflow and breakpoint bugs before handoff.
target_user: Product designers who hand off to engineers, and design engineers

icp.who: Product designers and design engineers at startups where handoff friction burns sprint time
icp.pain: Figma output is absolutely-positioned rectangles, so engineers rebuild every layout from scratch and responsive bugs appear at handoff
icp.buying_trigger: A responsive redesign or design-system project where layout handoff bugs keep eating sprint capacity

differentiators: Exports clean CSS Grid and Flexbox with zero absolute positioning
Layout audit flags overflow and breakpoint bugs before engineering ever sees the design
Layout-first canvas: structure is the primitive, not rectangles
proof_points: Layout audit caught 140 overflow bugs across alpha users' production sites
Exported CSS passes stylelint with zero warnings in the published demo repos

voice.sample_phrase: Layouts that ship, not rectangles that lie.

signals: Frequent breaking changes noted in alpha release notes

gaps: No integration with Figma import yet

confidence.notes: Product thesis is clear and demoable in alpha videos. All traction numbers are pre-launch and self-reported.
